$comment: Source is TypeScript now (src/host/*.ts, src/client/*.ts, plus src/shared/wire.ts — the wire contract both halves read, TYPE-ONLY), and every .ts file is type-checked unconditionally — `checkJs` only governs plain .js files, of which src/ has none (a .js under src/ would need a top-level '// @ts-check' pragma to be checked at all). strict is fully ON since 2026-10-03: noImplicitAny reached 0 (eight-domain migration) and flipped 2026-10-03, then strict:true itself was flipped with only one residual (a Set.next().value under noUncheckedIndexedAccess). The historical per-file graduation (tsconfig.strict-null.json) is retired as a gate and kept as a redundant double-check. strictNullChecks IS on project-wide since 2026-10-02 (docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md §8, the graduation-track endpoint): the per-file allowlist (tsconfig.strict-null.json) reached 100% of src, so the split is retired and the flag is stated here, in the one config that gates the push. noEmit:true means this check never produces artifacts — the build is tsdown's job (test/build-gate.mjs). Run it with `npm run typecheck`; since the 8 strict flags landed it is also part of `npm test` via test/typecheck-gate.mjs, which runs the tsc pinned in devDependencies (loud SKIP when typescript is absent, same rule as build-gate). erasableSyntaxOnly is TRUE and is the one flag here that exists for the TEST harness rather than for the types: `npm test` (the 30-item roster in test/suites.mjs, run by test/run-all.mjs) runs on bare `node` with no bundler, no loader and no dependencies (no tsx/jiti/vitest anywhere in package.json), importing `src/host/*.ts` directly (52 such imports), so Node's strip-only loader is the real compiler for every module a test can reach. Strip-only mode cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`) or angle-bracket assertions (`<T>expr`) — it fails at RUNTIME with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX — while plain tsc accepts all four, so without this flag a `.ts` file can typecheck clean and only explode when a suite imports it. The flag moves that to a compile-time error (TS1294). It costs nothing today: the sources are already fully erasable (verified by flipping the flag on and running both `npm run typecheck` and the full `npm test`, both green). Because test/typecheck-gate.mjs runs tsc on every push, this flag is enforced from the moment it lands — no gate change needed. tsconfig.strict-null.json `extends` this file, so it inherits the flag. Note it is NOT about .tsx: this project has none, and Node cannot execute .tsx under any flag anyway; the rule it encodes is simply that anything a bare-Node test imports must be erasable. Three more flags landed on 2026-10-20, and each one was MEASURED at zero diagnostics on this tree before it was written down: the recipe is `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --<flag>`, and a flag is only kept when that output is empty. A flag that needs code changes is a migration, not a switch. noImplicitReturns is TRUE: a function that can fall off the end without returning is a mistake the compiler can see, and it is NOT implied by strict (strict expands to exactly 9 flags and this is not among them — the same trap agnes-token-plan recorded in its own tsconfig). verbatimModuleSyntax is TRUE: it forces a type-only import to say so (`import type`), so the file says what the runtime will actually do. That matters here because the offline suites import src/host/*.ts directly on bare Node, where a type import that survives as a runtime import would break the loader. noUncheckedSideEffectImports is TRUE: a bare side-effect import whose module may not resolve is a startup-time landmine, and the flag turns it into a compile-time error. If one of these ever fires, that is the flag doing its job — fix the code, do not silence the flag.
